variants.title: Run one video job
variants.context: A video job parses the brief, plans temporal work before admission, generates latents across space-time patches or windows, decodes and inspects the sequence, then encodes, attests, and stores the asset.
variants.prompt: A creator submits a six second clip with a shot plan and two reference frames. Put the job stages in order.

items.text: Generate latents across space-time patches or windows while carrying anchors and overlap state through the timeline.
Decode and inspect per-frame quality, motion, continuity, identity, prompt alignment, and transition failures.
Plan temporal work: choose a native clip length or overlapping windows, reserve memory, and estimate service time before admission.
Encode the approved frames, attach provenance, persist decision evidence, and store the asset with a durable URL.
Parse the brief: normalize the prompt, references, aspect ratio, duration, shot plan, motion controls, and policy context.

variants.hint: One stage has to finish before the job can be admitted at all.
variants.explanation: Temporal planning happens before admission because window choice, memory class, and service time decide whether the job can be accepted.

variants.title: Run one video job
variants.context: A video job parses the brief, plans temporal work before admission, generates latents across space-time patches or windows, decodes and inspects the sequence, then encodes, attests, and stores the asset.
variants.prompt: One temporal window fails its seam check while the rest of the timeline passed. Put the retry steps in order.

items.text: Re-evaluate the transition against its neighboring windows.
Regenerate that window plus enough overlap to verify the seam.
Confirm deterministic ownership and an idempotent write before committing the window.
Identify the failed window from the checkpointed generation state.
Leave the rest of the timeline untouched and continue to encoding.

variants.hint: The retry scope is the failed unit plus whatever proves the boundary.
variants.explanation: Window checkpoints let a retry cover one failed window plus overlap instead of restarting the whole clip.

variants.title: Run one video job
variants.context: A video job parses the brief, plans temporal work before admission, generates latents across space-time patches or windows, decodes and inspects the sequence, then encodes, attests, and stores the asset.
variants.prompt: Trace one request through the service components. Put the components in the order they act.

items.text: GPU workers checkpoint bounded windows and emit progress without exposing incomplete assets.
The durable scheduler applies priority, quotas, deadlines, leases, cancellation, and backpressure before dispatch.
Evaluation and media decode, evaluate, encode, sign, store, and deliver only approved candidates.
API and policy validate tenant limits, references, conditions, rights attestations, and input policy.
The planner chooses model, windows, preview path, expected service time, memory class, and budget.

variants.hint: Admission cannot apply a budget it has not been given.
variants.explanation: The planner produces the estimate the scheduler admits against, which is why video serving is a capacity problem rather than one queue.

variants.title: Apply the safety controls
variants.context: Video safety is a chain of independent controls: an input gate before compute, an isolated generation boundary, an output gate across the decoded sequence, escalation to trained reviewers, provenance attachment, and a response path for takedown and rollback.
variants.prompt: A clip is generated and published under normal conditions. Put the controls in order.

items.text: Response: support takedown, credential revocation, model rollback, and affected-output discovery.
Output gate: inspect frames, transitions, audio, identity similarity, and text overlays across the sequence.
Provenance: attach model, edit, and origin assertions and retain the signing evidence.
Generation boundary: isolate untrusted intermediate assets and make cancellation and timeout deterministic.
Escalation: route uncertain or high-impact cases to trained reviewers with minimized exposure.
Input gate: classify the prompt and reference media and enforce policy before GPU admission.

variants.hint: One control runs before any accelerator time is spent.
variants.explanation: Controls apply before compute, across the decoded sequence, and at publication, because a thumbnail can look acceptable while the timeline does not.

variants.title: Apply the safety controls
variants.context: Video safety is a chain of independent controls: an input gate before compute, an isolated generation boundary, an output gate across the decoded sequence, escalation to trained reviewers, provenance attachment, and a response path for takedown and rollback.
variants.prompt: A request supplies a reference face and the finished clip resembles a public figure. Put the controls in order for that case.

items.text: Generation runs in isolation and the intermediate frames stay unexposed.
The output gate measures identity similarity across the decoded sequence rather than on one thumbnail.
The input gate classifies the reference media against identity and impersonation policy.
The response path revokes credentials and discovers other assets built from the same reference.
A trained reviewer receives the case with minimized exposure and a documented decision policy.

variants.hint: Identity risk exists at the input and again in the decoded frames.
variants.explanation: Input and output gates are independent controls, and the response path exists so an accepted mistake can still be found and revoked.

variants.title: Apply the safety controls
variants.context: Video safety is a chain of independent controls: an input gate before compute, an isolated generation boundary, an output gate across the decoded sequence, escalation to trained reviewers, provenance attachment, and a response path for takedown and rollback.
variants.prompt: A clip passes every frame-level filter, but the sequence as a whole violates policy. Put the steps in order.

items.text: The isolated worker produces the decoded sequence without exposing it.
The input gate finds nothing prohibited in the prompt or the references.
The output gate inspects transitions and temporal combinations that frame-only filters miss.
The case escalates to a reviewer because the harm exists only across time.
The decision, evaluator versions, and takedown path are recorded with the asset.

variants.hint: Harm that only exists across time cannot be seen one frame at a time.
variants.explanation: Video can create harmful content over time even when a sampled thumbnail looks acceptable, so the output gate reads the sequence.

variants.title: Size the video service
variants.context: Four quantities drive planning. Frame count is duration times generated frames per second. Offered GPU seconds per hour is arrivals per hour times service seconds per job. Required GPUs is that offered total divided by 3600 times target utilization. Cost per job is service seconds over 3600 times the GPU price.
variants.prompt: A profile receives 120 jobs per hour with a measured service time of 180 seconds per job, and the team targets 0.75 utilization. How many GPUs does the profile require?
variants.hint: Convert to GPU seconds per hour first, then leave headroom.
variants.explanation: Required GPUs is offered GPU seconds per hour divided by 3600 times target utilization, so headroom is part of the divisor rather than an afterthought.

mistakes.feedback: You divided by 3600 and skipped target utilization, leaving no headroom for retries or bursts.
You multiplied by target utilization instead of dividing by it.

variants.title: Size the video service
variants.context: Four quantities drive planning. Frame count is duration times generated frames per second. Offered GPU seconds per hour is arrivals per hour times service seconds per job. Required GPUs is that offered total divided by 3600 times target utilization. Cost per job is service seconds over 3600 times the GPU price.
variants.prompt: One job on that hardware measures 240 service seconds and the GPU costs 3.60 dollars per hour. What is the compute cost of one job?
variants.hint: The price is per hour and the measurement is in seconds.
variants.explanation: Cost per job is service seconds divided by 3600 times the GPU hourly price, so the unit conversion has to happen before the multiplication.

mistakes.feedback: You multiplied seconds by the hourly price without converting seconds to hours.

variants.title: Size the video service
variants.context: Four quantities drive planning. Frame count is duration times generated frames per second. Offered GPU seconds per hour is arrivals per hour times service seconds per job. Required GPUs is that offered total divided by 3600 times target utilization. Cost per job is service seconds over 3600 times the GPU price.
variants.prompt: A profile spends 240 dollars of GPU time on 100 submitted jobs. Only 60 of those are released, each as an 8 second clip. What is the cost per released second?
variants.hint: Only released output goes in the denominator.
variants.explanation: Cost per released second charges blocked outputs, retries, and abandoned previews to the work that actually shipped.

mistakes.feedback: That is cost per submitted job, not cost per released second.
You counted every submitted job as 8 released seconds, but blocked and abandoned jobs release nothing.

variants.title: Decide the production trade-off
variants.context: Long-form video is planned, not extended indefinitely. Shot structure, dataset rights, and preview economics are product decisions that a longer context window cannot settle.
variants.prompt: A team wants a 90 second multi-scene piece and proposes growing the context window until the whole piece fits one sample. What is the better plan?
options: Grow the context window so the model keeps every entity in view for the whole piece.
Generate one long clip and cut it afterward, so no seam evaluation is needed.
Plan shots, generate them as bounded units, and evaluate the transitions separately.
optionFeedback: Wrong: an ever-longer context window hides a real cut instead of planning one, and memory grows with frames.
Wrong: cutting after generation does not remove seams, it only stops anyone from measuring them.
Correct: bounded shots give retries a precise scope and make transitions their own measurable failure.
variants.hint: What scope should a retry have when one part fails?
variants.explanation: Long-form products plan shots, generate them as bounded units, and evaluate transitions separately, which also scopes the retry to one shot plus overlap.

variants.title: Decide the production trade-off
variants.context: Long-form video is planned, not extended indefinitely. Shot structure, dataset rights, and preview economics are product decisions that a longer context window cannot settle.
variants.prompt: A data team argues that publicly downloadable clips can be used for training because they were freely available. What should the rights review say?
options: Availability is sufficient as long as the dataset records the download date and source URL.
It is acceptable if the clips are used only for evaluation rather than for training.
Public availability is not a rights grant, so each source needs a documented rights basis.
optionFeedback: Wrong: acquisition metadata records where an item came from, not what uses were ever permitted.
Wrong: the manifest records allowed purposes explicitly, and evaluation is one of those purposes, not an exemption.
Correct: every source or dataset version needs a documented license or rights basis and allowed purposes.
variants.hint: What does the manifest have to record for every source?
variants.explanation: Public availability is not a rights grant. Sources need a documented rights basis, consent and identity restrictions, allowed purposes, and a tested deletion path.

variants.title: Decide the production trade-off
variants.context: Long-form video is planned, not extended indefinitely. Shot structure, dataset rights, and preview economics are product decisions that a longer context window cannot settle.
variants.prompt: A preview-first product finds that most previews are rejected and never reach a final render. What should the team measure and change?
options: Measure the preview approval rate, because rejected previews still consume capacity.
Ignore preview cost, because previews run at lower resolution than final renders.
Remove previews so every job spends its capacity once, at final quality.
optionFeedback: Correct: rejected previews are real GPU cost that releases nothing, so the approval rate is a required signal.
Wrong: cheaper per job is not free, and a low approval rate multiplies that cost across every attempt.
Wrong: removing previews moves the same rejections to full-price renders instead of cheaper ones.
variants.hint: Which jobs consume GPU seconds without releasing a second of video?
variants.explanation: Track cost per released second, because retries, blocked outputs, and abandoned previews are real product costs even though nothing ships.

variants.title: Match the mechanism
variants.context: The lesson names three generation patterns, four continuity layers, and three evaluation dimensions. Each carries a different responsibility, and picking the wrong one hides a failure instead of fixing it.
variants.prompt: A continuity plan has four layers. Match each layer with the mechanism that carries state at that scale.

pairs.label: Within a window
pairs.detail: Temporal attention, convolution, or space-time patch mixing shares evidence across nearby frames.

pairs.label: Across windows
pairs.detail: Overlap frames, cached latents, seeds, and reference embeddings carry state over a generation boundary.

pairs.label: Across shots
pairs.detail: A storyboard and entity manifest preserve identity while camera, location, or time change on purpose.

pairs.label: After generation
pairs.detail: Sequence-aware evaluators detect flicker, object disappearance, and duplicated limbs.

variants.hint: Ask what boundary each mechanism is carrying state across.
variants.explanation: Controlled continuity means a subject changes when the brief calls for it and not because the model lost track of scene state.

variants.title: Match the mechanism
variants.context: The lesson names three generation patterns, four continuity layers, and three evaluation dimensions. Each carries a different responsibility, and picking the wrong one hides a failure instead of fixing it.
variants.prompt: Three implementations are compared. Match each generation pattern with its defining trade-off.

pairs.label: Joint clip generation
pairs.detail: One bounded space-time sample with broad temporal context, but memory grows with frames and resolution.

pairs.label: Hierarchical generation
pairs.detail: Keyframes or a low-resolution timeline first, so each stage needs its own consistency checks.

pairs.label: Windowed extension
pairs.detail: Overlapping chunks carrying shared state, which supports longer clips but makes seams a named failure.

variants.hint: Ask what each pattern buys and what new failure it introduces.
variants.explanation: Each pattern trades temporal context against memory and introduces a different failure to measure, so the evaluation set follows the pattern chosen.

variants.title: Match the mechanism
variants.context: The lesson names three generation patterns, four continuity layers, and three evaluation dimensions. Each carries a different responsibility, and picking the wrong one hides a failure instead of fixing it.
variants.prompt: A release suite separates its scores. Match each evaluation dimension with what it measures.

pairs.label: Frame quality
pairs.detail: Sharpness, artifacts, text rendering, and anatomy on sampled and worst-case frames.

pairs.label: Temporal quality
pairs.detail: Flicker, object permanence, identity drift, camera adherence, and transition seams.

pairs.label: Contract quality
pairs.detail: Prompt alignment, reference fidelity, requested actions, duration, shot plan, and policy compliance.

variants.hint: One dimension only exists because the asset has a time axis.
variants.explanation: Separating the dimensions stops an average from hiding a critical failure, and a regressed required slice blocks promotion regardless of the mean.
